question: The researcher _____ discovered the new method received an international award.
options: which
who
whom
whose
explanation: Who refers to a person and functions as the subject of 'discovered'.

question: The engineer _____ we interviewed yesterday has accepted the position.
options: who
whom
whose
which
explanation: The relative pronoun is the object of 'interviewed', so whom is the formal choice.

question: The scientist _____ laboratory was damaged requested additional equipment.
options: who
whom
whose
which
explanation: Whose expresses possession: the laboratory belongs to the scientist.

question: The software _____ I installed yesterday has already stopped working.
options: who
whose
which
where
explanation: Which refers to a thing and functions as the object of 'installed'.

question: The lecturer _____ teaches advanced mathematics is absent today.
options: which
whose
whom
who
explanation: Who refers to a person and is the subject of 'teaches'.

question: The company _____ products are sold worldwide opened a new branch.
options: whose
which
whom
where
explanation: Whose expresses possession or relationship between the company and its products.

question: The student _____ I recommended for the scholarship has won it.
options: whose
whom
which
where
explanation: The student is the object of 'recommended', so whom is the formal object form.

question: The village _____ my grandparents were born has changed considerably.
options: which
where
whom
whose
explanation: Where refers to a place and means approximately 'in which'.

question: I still remember the evening _____ we received the announcement.
options: where
whose
when
whom
explanation: When refers to a time or occasion.

question: Nobody understood the reason _____ the manager resigned.
options: where
why
when
whom
explanation: Why is normally used after 'reason' to introduce the explanation.

question: The apartment _____ we rented last month is already being renovated.
options: who
where
which
whose
explanation: Which refers to the apartment and is the object of 'rented'.

question: The apartment _____ we lived for three years has been sold.
options: where
which
who
whose
explanation: Where refers to the place in which the living occurred.

question: The professor _____ research influenced the field retired last year.
options: whom
whose
which
where
explanation: Whose shows that the research belongs to or is associated with the professor.

question: The documentary _____ we watched last night was extremely informative.
options: whom
which
whose
where
explanation: Which refers to the documentary and functions as the object of 'watched'.

question: The athlete _____ broke the national record is only nineteen.
options: whom
whose
who
which
explanation: Who is the subject of 'broke' and refers to a person.

question: The candidate _____ the committee selected had extensive experience.
options: which
where
whom
whose
explanation: The candidate is the object of 'selected', making whom the formal choice.

question: The museum _____ we visited contains ancient manuscripts.
options: where
which
who
whose
explanation: Which is the object of 'visited'. The museum itself is being visited.

question: The museum _____ the manuscripts are displayed attracts thousands of visitors.
options: where
which
whom
whose
explanation: Where refers to the location in which the manuscripts are displayed.

question: The year _____ the university was founded is recorded in the archive.
options: where
why
when
whose
explanation: When refers to a particular year or time.

question: The reason _____ the experiment failed remains unclear.
options: when
which
why
where
explanation: Why commonly follows 'reason' and introduces its explanation.

question: The students _____ completed the assignment early were allowed to leave.
options: whom
which
who
whose
explanation: Who is the subject of 'completed' and refers to the students.

question: The books _____ the professor recommended are available in the library.
options: who
where
which
whose
explanation: Which refers to books and functions as the object of 'recommended'.

question: The employee _____ performance improved dramatically received a promotion.
options: whose
whom
which
where
explanation: Whose expresses the relationship between the employee and the performance.

question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
options: The man which called me is my uncle.
The man whom called me is my uncle.
The man who called me is my uncle.
The man whose called me is my uncle.
explanation: Who is required because the relative pronoun is the subject of 'called'.

question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
options: The woman who I met her was a doctor.
The woman whom I met was a doctor.
The woman which I met was a doctor.
The woman whose I met was a doctor.
explanation: Whom correctly functions as the object of 'met', and no extra object pronoun is needed.

question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
options: The computer that I repaired is working again.
The computer who I repaired is working again.
The computer whom I repaired is working again.
The computer where I repaired is working again.
explanation: That can refer to things in a defining relative clause and functions as the object of 'repaired'.

question: Which sentence correctly uses a non-defining relative clause?
options: My sister that lives abroad is a doctor.
My sister, that lives abroad, is a doctor.
My sister, who lives abroad, is a doctor.
My sister who lives abroad, is a doctor.
explanation: Non-defining clauses require commas and normally use who rather than that.

question: Which sentence correctly uses a defining relative clause?
options: The students, who passed the exam received certificates.
The students who passed the exam received certificates.
The students who passed the exam, received certificates.
The students, that passed the exam, received certificates.
explanation: A defining relative clause provides essential information and does not use commas.

question: In which sentence can the relative pronoun be omitted?
options: The man who lives upstairs is a doctor.
The student who won the prize is absent.
The book that I borrowed is missing.
The woman who teaches us is kind.
explanation: That is the object of 'borrowed', so it can be omitted: 'The book I borrowed'.

question: Which sentence contains a relative pronoun that cannot normally be omitted?
options: The movie which we watched was long.
The teacher who helped me was patient.
The book that I bought was expensive.
The car which I repaired is working.
explanation: Who is the subject of 'helped', so it cannot normally be omitted.

question: Choose the best formal completion: 'The professor to _____ I spoke was very helpful.'
options: who
whom
which
that
explanation: After the preposition 'to', whom is used formally for a person.

question: Choose the correct formal sentence.
options: The organization for that she works is international.
The organization for whom she works is international.
The organization for which she works is international.
The organization which for she works is international.
explanation: Which refers to the organization, and the formal structure is 'for which'.

question: Choose the correct formal sentence.
options: The house in that they live is large.
The house in which they live is large.
The house in whom they live is large.
The house which in they live is large.
explanation: The formal structure for a thing after 'in' is 'in which'.

question: Which sentence is grammatically correct in informal English?
options: The person to who I spoke was helpful.
The person who I spoke to was helpful.
The person to that I spoke was helpful.
The person whom I spoke to him was helpful.
explanation: In informal English, the preposition can appear at the end: 'who I spoke to'.

question: Which sentence correctly uses 'that'?
options: My car, that is very old, needs repair.
The car that I bought is very reliable.
The car, that I bought yesterday, is reliable.
My brother, that lives abroad, is a doctor.
explanation: That is appropriate in a defining relative clause.

question: Which sentence contains an incorrect use of 'where'?
options: The town where I grew up is quiet.
The school where I studied has expanded.
The house where I bought is expensive.
The office where she works is nearby.
explanation: In 'I bought the house', house is the object of 'bought', so which or that is required.

question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The day which we met was memorable.
The day when we met was memorable.
The day where we met was memorable.
The day whom we met was memorable.
explanation: When correctly expresses the time relationship with 'the day'.

question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The day when I remember was unforgettable.
The day where I remember was unforgettable.
The day which I remember was unforgettable.
The day whom I remember was unforgettable.
explanation: Here 'day' is the object of 'remember', so which is appropriate.

question: Which sentence correctly uses 'why'?
options: The reason where he left is unknown.
The reason when he left is unknown.
The reason why he left is unknown.
The reason whom he left is unknown.
explanation: Why is normally associated with the noun 'reason'.

question: Which sentence is correct?
options: The reason which he resigned is unclear.
The reason why he resigned is unclear.
The reason where he resigned is unclear.
The reason whom he resigned is unclear.
explanation: Why appropriately introduces the reason for his resignation.

question: Choose the correct sentence using 'whose'.
options: The student who's phone was stolen reported it.
The student whose phone was stolen reported it.
The student who phone was stolen reported it.
The student whom phone was stolen reported it.
explanation: Whose expresses possession; who's means 'who is' or 'who has'.

question: Which sentence correctly uses 'what'?
options: The book what I bought was expensive.
What I bought was expensive.
The book what I bought it was expensive.
What the book I bought was expensive.
explanation: What introduces a free relative clause without a separate antecedent.

question: Which sentence is incorrect?
options: What she said surprised everyone.
The book which she recommended was useful.
The book what she recommended was useful.
Whatever she chooses will be acceptable.
explanation: What normally cannot follow an existing antecedent such as 'the book'.

question: In the sentence 'What you need is on the desk,' what does 'what you need' mean?
options: The person who needs you
The thing that you need
The place where you need something
The reason why you need something
explanation: What commonly means 'the thing that' in a free relative clause.

question: Choose the correct completion: '_____ arrives first can enter the room.'
options: Which
Whom
Whoever
Whose
explanation: Whoever means 'any person who' and can function as the subject.

question: Choose the correct completion: 'Take _____ you need from the cupboard.'
options: whatever
whoever
whichever
whose
explanation: Whatever refers to anything that is needed.

question: Choose the best completion when selecting one option from a limited set: 'Choose _____ answer you think is correct.'
options: whoever
whatever
whichever
whose
explanation: Whichever refers to any one choice from a limited set.

question: Which sentence correctly demonstrates agreement inside a relative clause?
options: The students who studies hard usually succeed.
The student who study hard usually succeeds.
The students who study hard usually succeed.
The student who study hard usually succeed.
explanation: The antecedent 'students' is plural, so the relative-clause verb is 'study'.

question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The student who study mathematics is successful.
The student who studies mathematics is successful.
The student who studying mathematics is successful.
The student who studied mathematics are successful.
explanation: The singular antecedent 'student' requires 'studies'.

question: Which sentence correctly uses a reduced active relative clause?
options: The man standing near the door is my teacher.
The man stood near the door is my teacher.
The man stands near the door is my teacher.
The man whom standing near the door is my teacher.
explanation: 'Who is standing' can be reduced to 'standing' when the relative pronoun is the subject.

question: Choose the reduced form of 'The books that were written by the professor are valuable.'
options: The books writing by the professor are valuable.
The books written by the professor are valuable.
The books wrote by the professor are valuable.
The books which writing by the professor are valuable.
explanation: A passive relative clause with 'were written' can be reduced to 'written'.

question: Which sentence correctly combines the two ideas: 'The woman is a scientist. Her research won an award.'?
options: The woman who research won an award is a scientist.
The woman whose research won an award is a scientist.
The woman whom research won an award is a scientist.
The woman which research won an award is a scientist.
explanation: Whose correctly expresses possession between the woman and her research.

question: Which sentence correctly combines: 'I visited a city. I was born in the city.'?
options: I visited the city who I was born.
I visited the city where I was born.
I visited the city whom I was born.
I visited the city whose I was born.
explanation: Where introduces the location in which the speaker was born.

question: Which sentence correctly combines: 'I remember the year. We graduated in that year.'?
options: I remember the year where we graduated.
I remember the year when we graduated.
I remember the year who we graduated.
I remember the year whose we graduated.
explanation: When refers to the time expressed by 'the year'.

question: Which sentence correctly combines: 'She explained the reason. She left because of that reason.'?
options: She explained the reason why she left.
She explained the reason where she left.
She explained the reason whom she left.
She explained the reason when she left.
explanation: Why introduces the reason for her leaving.

question: Which sentence correctly combines: 'The teacher helped me. I thanked the teacher.'?
options: The teacher whom helped me was thanked.
The teacher who I thanked helped me.
The teacher whose I thanked helped me.
The teacher which I thanked helped me.
explanation: Who refers to the teacher, while the teacher is the object of 'thanked'.

question: Which sentence correctly combines: 'The teacher helped me. The teacher is experienced.'?
options: The teacher whom helped me is experienced.
The teacher who helped me is experienced.
The teacher which helped me is experienced.
The teacher whose helped me is experienced.
explanation: Who is the subject of 'helped'.

question: Which sentence contains an unnecessary extra pronoun?
options: The man whom I met was friendly.
The man who I met was friendly.
The man who I met him was friendly.
The man I met was friendly.
explanation: The relative pronoun already represents the object, so 'him' is unnecessary.

question: Which sentence contains a double-object error?
options: The book which I bought is expensive.
The book that I bought is expensive.
The book I bought is expensive.
The book which I bought it is expensive.
explanation: Which already functions as the object of 'bought', so 'it' is unnecessary.

question: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: The person to whom I spoke was helpful.
The person to that I spoke was helpful.
The person to who I spoke was helpful.
The person to whom I spoke to was helpful.
explanation: The formal structure is preposition + whom for a person.

question: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: The company for whom he works manufactures computers.
The company for which he works manufactures computers.
The company for that he works manufactures computers.
The company for who he works manufactures computers.
explanation: Which is used for a thing or organization after the preposition 'for'.

question: Which sentence correctly uses a non-defining relative clause referring to a whole preceding clause?
options: He missed the bus that made him late.
He missed the bus, which made him late.
He missed the bus, that made him late.
He missed the bus which made him late.
explanation: Comma + which can refer to the whole preceding situation: the fact that he missed the bus.

question: In 'She passed the examination, which surprised everyone,' what does 'which' refer to?
options: She
The examination only
The fact that she passed the examination
Everyone
explanation: Comma + which can comment on the entire preceding clause.

question: Which sentence correctly uses a non-defining relative clause?
options: My father who lives in Hawassa is a teacher.
My father, who lives in Hawassa, is a teacher.
My father, that lives in Hawassa, is a teacher.
My father which lives in Hawassa is a teacher.
explanation: The extra information is non-defining, so commas and who are appropriate.

question: Which sentence changes the meaning by making the relative clause defining?
options: The students who passed the exam received certificates.
The students, who passed the exam, received certificates.
Both sentences necessarily have exactly the same meaning.
Neither sentence is grammatically possible.
explanation: Without commas, the clause identifies which students received certificates.

question: Which sentence suggests that all the students passed the exam?
options: The students who passed the exam received certificates.
The students, who passed the exam, received certificates.
The students that passed the exam received certificates.
The students whom passed the exam received certificates.
explanation: The non-defining clause between commas adds information about the already identified students.

question: Which relative word is normally unsuitable in a non-defining clause?
options: who
which
whose
that
explanation: That is normally not used in non-defining relative clauses.

question: Which sentence is correct?
options: My laptop, that is quite old, still works.
My laptop, which is quite old, still works.
My laptop which, is quite old still works.
My laptop, who is quite old, still works.
explanation: Which is appropriate for a non-defining clause referring to a thing.

question: Which sentence correctly uses 'that' in a defining clause referring to a person?
options: The doctor that treated me was excellent.
The doctor, that treated me, was excellent.
The doctor that, treated me was excellent.
The doctor whom treated me was excellent.
explanation: That can refer to people in defining relative clauses.

question: Which sentence correctly uses 'that' for an animal?
options: The horse that won the race was extremely fast.
The horse, that won the race, was extremely fast.
The horse whom won the race was extremely fast.
The horse where won the race was extremely fast.
explanation: That can refer to animals in defining relative clauses.

question: Which sentence uses 'who' appropriately for an animal treated as an individual?
options: The dog who saved the child became famous.
The dog who its owner sold became famous.
The dog whom saved the child became famous.
The dog whose saved the child became famous.
explanation: Who can be used for an animal when it is treated personally or as an individual.

question: Which sentence correctly uses a preposition at the end?
options: The colleague whom I worked with was experienced.
The colleague with whom I worked with was experienced.
The colleague with that I worked was experienced.
The colleague who with I worked was experienced.
explanation: In informal English, the preposition can remain at the end: 'whom I worked with'.

question: Which sentence correctly uses the formal alternative to 'The colleague whom I worked with...'?
options: The colleague with whom I worked was experienced.
The colleague with that I worked was experienced.
The colleague with who I worked was experienced.
The colleague whom with I worked was experienced.
explanation: Formal English places the preposition before whom: 'with whom'.

question: Which sentence correctly uses 'where' rather than 'which'?
options: The laboratory where we conducted the experiment was modern.
The laboratory where we used yesterday was modern.
The laboratory where I repaired was modern.
The laboratory where I visited was modern.
explanation: Where refers to the place in which the experiment was conducted.

question: Which sentence correctly uses 'which' rather than 'where'?
options: The restaurant where we visited was crowded.
The restaurant which we visited was crowded.
The restaurant where we ate it was crowded.
The restaurant where we visited it was crowded.
explanation: The restaurant is the object of 'visited', so which is appropriate.

question: Which sentence correctly uses 'in which'?
options: The building in which they work is historic.
The building in that they work is historic.
The building in whom they work is historic.
The building in where they work is historic.
explanation: In which is the formal equivalent of 'where' for a thing or place.

question: Which sentence correctly uses 'on which'?
options: The day on which we met changed my life.
The day on that we met changed my life.
The day on where we met changed my life.
The day on whom we met changed my life.
explanation: On which is the formal structure for a time relationship involving a day.

question: Which sentence correctly uses 'for which'?
options: The reason for which he resigned was never explained.
The reason for that he resigned was never explained.
The reason for where he resigned was never explained.
The reason for whom he resigned was never explained.
explanation: For which is a formal alternative to 'why' after 'reason'.

question: Which sentence correctly uses 'what' rather than 'which'?
options: The information what I need is missing.
What I need is missing.
The information what I need it is missing.
What the information I need is missing.
explanation: What introduces a free relative clause without a separate antecedent.

question: Which sentence incorrectly uses a relative pronoun because an antecedent is already present?
options: What he said was surprising.
Whatever he says will be recorded.
The statement which he made was surprising.
The statement what he made was surprising.
explanation: The antecedent 'statement' is already present, so which or that should be used instead of what.

question: Which sentence correctly uses 'whoever'?
options: Whoever finishes the task first will receive the prize.
Whoever the task first will receive the prize.
Whoever which finishes the task will receive the prize.
Whoever whose finishes the task will receive the prize.
explanation: Whoever means 'any person who' and functions as the subject.

question: Which sentence correctly uses 'whatever'?
options: Whatever you decide will be acceptable.
Whatever who you decide will be acceptable.
Whatever which you decide will be acceptable.
Whatever whose you decide will be acceptable.
explanation: Whatever means 'anything that' or 'no matter what'.

question: Which sentence correctly uses 'whichever'?
options: Whichever of these two routes you choose will work.
Whoever of these two routes you choose will work.
Whatever of these two routes you choose will work.
Whose of these two routes you choose will work.
explanation: Whichever refers to one choice from a limited set.

question: Which sentence contains a subject-verb agreement error inside the relative clause?
options: The engineer who designs the system is experienced.
The engineers who design the system are experienced.
The engineer who design the system is experienced.
The engineers who design the system work efficiently.
explanation: The singular antecedent 'engineer' requires 'designs'.

question: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: The group of students who studies together is successful.
The group of students who study together is successful.
The group of students who studies together are successful.
The group of students which study together are successful.
explanation: Here 'who' refers to the plural 'students', so 'study' is correct; the main subject 'group' takes 'is'.

question: Which sentence correctly uses a defining relative clause with no commas?
options: The employees who completed the training received certificates.
The employees, who completed the training, received certificates.
The employees who completed the training, received certificates.
The employees, who completed the training received certificates.
explanation: The relative clause identifies which employees, so it is defining and requires no commas.

question: Which sentence correctly uses a non-defining relative clause?
options: Ethiopia which has a long history attracts many researchers.
Ethiopia, which has a long history, attracts many researchers.
Ethiopia that has a long history attracts many researchers.
Ethiopia, that has a long history, attracts many researchers.
explanation: The proper noun already identifies the country, so the additional information is non-defining.

question: Which sentence is grammatically incorrect because the relative pronoun is omitted as the subject?
options: The book I bought was expensive.
The person I met was friendly.
The man lives next door is a doctor.
The movie we watched was excellent.
explanation: The omitted relative pronoun would be the subject of 'lives', so it cannot normally be omitted.

question: Which sentence correctly omits the relative pronoun?
options: The scientist discovered the formula won an award.
The scientist I interviewed won an award.
The scientist works here won an award.
The scientist invented the formula won an award.
explanation: In 'the scientist I interviewed', the omitted relative pronoun is the object of 'interviewed'.

question: Which sentence contains a correct formal relative structure?
options: The researcher with whom I collaborated published a paper.
The researcher with that I collaborated published a paper.
The researcher whom with I collaborated published a paper.
The researcher with who I collaborated published a paper.
explanation: With whom is the formal structure for a person after the preposition 'with'.

question: Which sentence contains an incorrect relative pronoun?
options: The professor whose lecture I attended was excellent.
The professor whom I contacted replied quickly.
The professor which teaches physics is absent.
The professor who teaches physics is absent.
explanation: Which is normally used for things and animals, not people.

question: Which sentence contains an incorrect use of 'whom'?
options: The person whom I invited arrived early.
The person to whom I spoke was helpful.
The person whom called me was helpful.
The person whom we interviewed was qualified.
explanation: Whom is an object, but here the relative word is the subject of 'called', so who is required.

question: Which sentence contains an incorrect use of 'whose'?
options: The student whose laptop broke reported the problem.
The company whose offices are nearby hired new workers.
The teacher whose helped me was kind.
The woman whose son is a doctor lives here.
explanation: Whose must be followed by a possessed noun, not directly by the verb 'helped'.

question: Which sentence correctly uses 'whose' with a non-human antecedent?
options: The company whose headquarters are in Addis Ababa expanded rapidly.
The company whose is in Addis Ababa expanded rapidly.
The company whose it operates in Addis Ababa expanded rapidly.
The company whom headquarters are in Addis Ababa expanded rapidly.
explanation: Whose can express possession or association with things and organizations.

question: Which sentence correctly uses a reduced passive relative clause?
options: The documents submitted yesterday are being reviewed.
The documents submitting yesterday are being reviewed.
The documents submit yesterday are being reviewed.
The documents which submitting yesterday are being reviewed.
explanation: 'Which were submitted' can be reduced to 'submitted'.

question: Which sentence correctly uses a reduced active relative clause?
options: The students studying in the library are preparing for exams.
The students studied in the library are preparing for exams.
The students study in the library are preparing for exams.
The students whom studying in the library are preparing for exams.
explanation: 'Students who are studying' can be reduced to 'students studying'.

question: Which sentence has the correct relative-clause structure?
options: The woman who I believe is the manager arrived.
The woman whom I believe is the manager arrived.
The woman which I believe is the manager arrived.
The woman whose I believe is the manager arrived.
explanation: Who is the subject of 'is the manager'; 'I believe' is inserted before the predicate.

question: Which sentence correctly uses 'which' to refer to a thing in a non-defining clause?
options: The laptop, which I bought last year, still works perfectly.
The laptop, that I bought last year, still works perfectly.
The laptop which, I bought last year still works perfectly.
The laptop, who I bought last year, still works perfectly.
explanation: Which is appropriate for a non-defining clause referring to a thing.

question: Which sentence correctly uses an omitted object relative pronoun?
options: The article I read yesterday was controversial.
The article I wrote yesterday was controversial.
The article I published yesterday was controversial.
All of the above.
explanation: In each sentence, the article is the object of the verb, so the relative pronoun can be omitted.

question: Which sentence correctly uses 'where' and not 'when'?
options: This is the laboratory where the experiment was conducted.
This is the laboratory when the experiment was conducted.
This is the laboratory whose the experiment was conducted.
This is the laboratory whom the experiment was conducted.
explanation: Where refers to the location of the experiment.
